page: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is a memory-optimized instance featuring a single dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor core operating at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core fall into the bottom 10% to 25%. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is average, while read-only memory bandwidth is weaker, particularly for larger uncached blocks.

This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high memory-to-CPU ratios at a small scale without the overhead of multi-core pricing. It is suitable for lightweight database operations, single-threaded applications, Redis caching, and basic text processing tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU execution and DDR5 memory speeds.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is a memory-optimized instance powered by a single dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor core running at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and the Nitro hypervisor, it features 8.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, providing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU performance, though multi-core and memory read bandwidth metrics are lower due to the single-vCPU limitation. This server is qualitatively cost-effective for small-scale, memory-intensive workloads, such as lightweight database operations, single-threaded data processing, and Redis caching, where dedicated CPU allocation and modern DDR5 memory are required without the cost of larger multi-core configurations.
